# 9ui rulebook

The rules every 9ui component follows, so the library reads as if one person designed it. This is 9ui's house style. After you import it, it is yours: change any rule, and record the change in `decisions.md`.

## Files

| File | What it covers |
|---|---|
| `surfaces.md` | Radius, fields, popups, modals, cards, fills, colour tokens |
| `states.md` | Focus, hover, pressed, highlighted, open, disabled, invalid, read-only, cursor |
| `sizing.md` | Heights, type, touch sizes, hit areas, icons, list popups, text parts |
| `motion.md` | Curves, durations, popups, modals, expand and collapse, reduced motion |
| `content.md` | Long text, missing data, popups at small widths |
| `rtl.md` | Right-to-left layout |
| `accessibility.md` | What is required, what is optional |
| `code.md` | File shape, typing, slots, variants, naming |
| `registry.md` | Demos, docs pages and registry entries. Applies only to projects that publish a registry |
| `decisions.md` | Every change to a rule, every exception, every accepted deviation from a standard |

## How a rule is written

```md
### MOT-2 Popups scale and fade from their trigger

One or two sentences that state the rule.

- **Recipe:** the classes or values that implement it.
- **Applies to:** the roles or components it covers.
- **Why:** the reason, so the rule can be judged when a case does not fit.
- **Standard:** the standard it implements, if any (for example `STD-M7`).
- **Exceptions:** Component: reason.
```

- The id never changes, even when the rule does. Removed rules keep their heading with "Removed" and a date.
- A rule with a **Standard** line implements a general standard the skills always check. You can still change it; the change is listed as an accepted deviation in every report.
- A rule without one is house style. Change it freely; after that, only components that do not follow the new value are reported.
- **Exceptions** are components that break the rule on purpose. An exception with a reason is not reported.

## Tailwind

Tailwind reads this folder like any other source file. To keep class names that appear only here out of your CSS, exclude it in your main stylesheet, with the path relative to that file:

```css
@source not "../.rulebook";
```

## Roles

Rules apply to roles, not to component names. A new component takes the rules of the role it plays.

| Role | Examples |
|---|---|
| Button-sized control | Button, Toggle, Select trigger, Tabs tab |
| Text field | Input, Textarea, Number Field, OTP Field, Input Group, Combobox chips |
| Small control | Checkbox, Radio, Switch, Slider thumb |
| List popup | Menu, Context Menu, Menubar, Select, Combobox, Autocomplete |
| Content popup | Popover, Preview Card, Tooltip, Navigation Menu |
| Modal | Dialog, Alert Dialog |
| Edge panel | Sheet, Drawer, bottom Dialog on small screens |
| Card surface | Card, Alert, Table frame, Toolbar, Menubar bar |
| List item | Menu item, Select item, Command item |
| Indicator | Check mark, radio dot, Progress, Meter, Badge, Spinner |

# Surfaces

### SUR-1 Radius follows the role

Each role has one radius. A component never picks its own.

- **Recipe:** controls and popups `rounded-lg`; `sm` controls `rounded-[min(var(--radius-md),0.75rem)]`; `xs` controls `rounded-[min(var(--radius-md),0.625rem)]`; list items and chips `rounded-sm`; cards and containers `rounded-xl`; modals `--radius-xl`; edge panels `--radius-2xl`; tracks and badges `rounded-full`.
- **Why:** radius is the fastest way to tell that two parts belong to the same family.
- **Exceptions:** Tooltip: `rounded-md`, it is a small inverted label, not a popup surface. Tabs tab: `rounded-md`, it sits inside the tab list (see `SUR-2`). Command and Emoji Picker: `rounded-xl`, they are standalone containers that can also be placed in a popup. Sidebar badge and Sidebar action buttons: `rounded-md`, they sit inside a menu row. Dialog and Alert Dialog in bottom mode: keep the modal radius on their top corners, as Drawer does. Checkbox: `rounded-[min(var(--radius-sm),0.25rem)]`, so a 16px box never turns into a circle.

### SUR-2 Nested radii keep their role

Nested parts use fixed radius tokens, never a value computed from their container. Concentric (inner = outer minus border minus padding) is the reference, not a requirement.

- **Recipe:** a child may be up to 3px rounder than concentric and at most 1px squarer. Do not square a child or change padding to reach an exact fit.
- **Applies to:** items in list popups, tabs in a tab list, buttons in a toolbar, search fields inside popups.
- **Why:** re-deriving each child from its container breaks down in containers with mixed children, and the visible error inside this band is about 1px.

### SUR-3 Field surface

- **Recipe:** `bg-input shadow-xs`, a 1px `border-border` edge, and a 1px edge highlight: black 6% under the bottom edge in light, white 8% along the top edge in dark. The shadow and highlight are removed when the field is disabled, read-only or invalid; the highlight is also removed on focus.
- **Applies to:** text fields, Select trigger.
- **Why:** the highlight gives the field depth; on focus the ring takes over, and a disabled or invalid field should look flat.
- **Exceptions:** Input, Textarea, OTP Field: native inputs cannot render `::before`, so they draw the edge with `inset-ring-1` and the highlight with `inset-shadow`. The result must match the pseudo-element version.

### SUR-4 Outlined control surface

Outlined controls use the field surface, and drop the shadow and highlight when they are pressed, checked, disabled or invalid.

- **Recipe:** `border-border bg-input shadow-xs` plus the `before:` highlight, gated with `not-active` and `not-data-disabled` on buttons and toggles, and with `not-data-checked` and `not-aria-invalid` on Checkbox and Radio.
- **Applies to:** Button `outline` and `destructive-outline`, Toggle `outline`, Checkbox, Radio.

### SUR-5 Popup surface

- **Recipe:** `bg-popover text-popover-foreground rounded-lg border shadow-md`, no blur. Light: `not-dark:shadow-[0_1px_--theme(--color-black/6%),var(--shadow-md)]`. Dark: the `edge-highlight-*` utility with the popup's radius, for example `dark:edge-highlight-lg` or `dark:edge-highlight-(--popover-radius)`.
- **Applies to:** list popups and content popups.
- **Why:** one edge treatment on every floating surface, drawn with one shared utility.
- **Exceptions:** Tooltip: inverted, `bg-foreground text-background`, no border. Select: `ring-1 ring-border` in place of `border`, with the same highlights drawn as shadow layers under the ring, so the popup can line up with its trigger.

### SUR-6 Modal surface

- **Recipe:** backdrop `bg-black/30 dark:bg-black/50 supports-backdrop-filter:backdrop-blur-xs`; panel `bg-popover shadow-lg` with the popup edge treatment; footer `bg-muted/50 border-t`; a panel under a nested one dims with `brightness-90 dark:brightness-75`.
- **Applies to:** modals and edge panels.

### SUR-7 Card surface

- **Recipe:** `rounded-xl border shadow-xs bg-card text-card-foreground` plus the `before:` edge highlight.
- **Applies to:** Card, Alert, Table frame, Toolbar, Menubar bar, floating and inset Sidebar panels.
- **Exceptions:** tinted Alert variants: 5% of the tone mixed into the card colour, for example `bg-[color-mix(in_oklab,var(--warning)_5%,var(--card))]`, so the tint sits on the card colour and keeps the dark surface lift.

### SUR-8 Primary fills

A button-sized primary fill carries a white 20% top highlight. Indicators 20px and under stay flat.

- **Applies to:** highlight on Button `default` and the selected Calendar day; flat on checked Checkbox, Radio, Switch, Badge, and Slider, Progress and Meter fills.
- **Why:** a highlight on a small indicator reads as noise.

### SUR-9 Colours come from tokens

No raw colours in components.

- **Recipe:** theme tokens only. Black and white with alpha are allowed for edge highlights, shadows and backdrops.
- **Why:** presets and dark mode change tokens; a raw colour does not follow.
- **Exceptions:** Slider thumb: white in both themes, it is a physical knob. Number Field scrub cursor: black with a white outline, like a system cursor.

### SUR-10 No `!` modifier

Components never use Tailwind's `!` modifier. To override a class, pass the same variant chain so `tailwind-merge` replaces it.

- **Why:** `!` makes a class impossible to override from `className`.
- **Standard:** `STD-K5`
- **Exceptions:** Vaul: its library injects unlayered CSS that only `!` can beat.

# States

### STA-1 Focus ring

- **Recipe:** `outline-none focus-visible:ring-3 focus-visible:ring-ring/50`. Add `focus-visible:border-ring` (or `focus-visible:inset-ring-ring`) when the element has a visible edge. A composite field puts the ring on its wrapper with a `has-` variant that matches its focused input, for example `has-[[data-slot=input-group-control]:focus-visible]:border-ring`.
- **Applies to:** every focusable element.
- **Standard:** `STD-A3`
- **Exceptions:** list items: they show `data-highlighted` instead of a ring. Accordion trigger: adds a 1px inset outline to the ring, because the accordion clips a ring drawn outside the trigger.

### STA-2 The keyboard focus ring does not fade in

- **Recipe:** `focus-visible:duration-0` on controls that have `box-shadow` in their transition list.
- **Why:** the ring is a box shadow, so it would otherwise animate in over 150ms and feel late.
- **Exceptions:** text fields: `:focus-visible` also matches on click there, and the ring fades on purpose.

### STA-3 Hover

- **Recipe:** neutral controls `hover:bg-accent hover:text-accent-foreground dark:hover:bg-accent/50`; filled controls drop their fill to 80% (`hover:bg-primary/80`); tinted `/20`, dark `/30`; text links `hover:text-foreground`. Text fields and list items have no hover.
- **Exceptions:** Toggle and Sidebar menu buttons: `hover:bg-accent/50` in both themes, so hover stays weaker than the pressed or active fill.

### STA-4 Pressed

Every pressable responds on pointer-down, with a scale and an instant colour step.

- **Recipe:** scale `motion-safe:active:scale-98` on buttons and toggles, `scale-95` on small controls (Checkbox, Radio, Calendar day, emoji). Colour, preferably through `[&:active]:` so it beats hover: neutral buttons `[&:active]:bg-foreground/15 dark:[&:active]:bg-accent`; small controls and members of dense sets `bg-foreground/10`; default fill `/75`; secondary `/60`; tinted `/30`, dark `/40`. Colour is left out of the transition while pressed (an `active:` transition list without colour).
- **Why:** the colour step is what shows on small targets and under reduced motion, where scale is invisible or off.
- **Standard:** `STD-M10`
- **Exceptions:** triggers that open a list on press (`[aria-haspopup=menu]`, `[aria-haspopup=listbox]`, `[role=combobox]`) and link-style buttons do not scale. Controls joined in a group cancel the scale. Members of dense sets (tabs, accordion triggers, menubar and navigation triggers, sidebar buttons) change colour only.

### STA-5 Highlighted list item

- **Recipe:** `data-highlighted:bg-accent data-highlighted:text-accent-foreground rounded-sm cursor-default outline-none`, no transition.
- **Applies to:** every item in a list popup.
- **Why:** the highlight follows the pointer and arrow keys; easing it makes the list feel slow.

### STA-6 Open trigger

- **Recipe:** `data-popup-open:bg-accent data-popup-open:text-accent-foreground`, at 50% in dark mode (`dark:data-popup-open:bg-accent/50`) on standalone triggers. Button uses `aria-expanded:` for the same fill.

### STA-7 Disabled

- **Recipe:** opacity 50. Buttons, tabs and items add `pointer-events-none`; form controls add `cursor-not-allowed`; labels use `text-foreground/50`. Style `aria-disabled` too when the primitive uses it.
- **Exceptions:** Accordion trigger: `cursor-not-allowed` in place of `pointer-events-none`.

### STA-8 Invalid

Invalid at rest is a red edge only. The red ring appears on keyboard focus.

- **Recipe:** `aria-invalid:border-destructive/60` (or `aria-invalid:inset-ring-destructive/60`), `aria-invalid:ring-destructive/30 dark:aria-invalid:ring-destructive/40` together with the focus ring. Labels `data-invalid:text-destructive`. In arbitrary selectors write `[aria-invalid=true]`, never bare `[aria-invalid]`.
- **Why:** a form full of resting red rings is louder than the error it reports. Bare `[aria-invalid]` also matches `aria-invalid="false"`.
- **Standard:** `STD-K4`

### STA-9 Read-only field

- **Recipe:** `bg-transparent`, no shadow, no edge highlight, text at full strength and selectable.
- **Applies to:** Input, Textarea, OTP Field, Number Field, Input Group.
- **Why:** a read-only field shows a value that can be copied but not edited, so it loses the "type here" surface.

### STA-10 Cursor

- **Recipe:** `cursor-pointer` on buttons and button-like triggers, `cursor-default` on list items, `cursor-not-allowed` on disabled form controls. Field-like triggers, such as the Select trigger, keep the default cursor, like the text fields they sit beside.

# Sizing and type

### SIZ-1 Height scale

One scale for every row control. Each size grows one step on touch devices.

- **Recipe:** fine pointer, then `any-pointer-coarse:`: xs `h-6`, `h-7`; sm `h-7`, `h-8`; default `h-8`, `h-9`; lg `h-9`, `h-10`; xl `h-10`, `h-11`. List items `min-h-7`, `min-h-9`. Checkbox, Radio and Slider thumb `size-4`, `size-5`.
- **Why:** a Button next to an Input of the same size must line up.

### SIZ-2 Size coverage

Every row control takes `size` with `sm | default | lg`. Button also has `xs` and `xl`.

- **Applies to:** Button, Toggle, Input, Input Group, Select trigger, Number Field, OTP Field, Combobox chips, Phone Input.
- **Exceptions:** Textarea: no `size`, it has no fixed height.

### SIZ-3 Control type

- **Recipe:** `text-sm font-medium`; `sm` controls `text-[0.8rem]`; `xs` `text-xs`; `gap-1.5 px-2.5` at the default size. Only `font-medium` and `font-normal` are used. No px font sizes and nothing under 11px.
- **Exceptions:** Input: `px-2.75`, so its text lines up optically with a Select trigger's.

### SIZ-4 Touch text

Interactive text grows to 16px on touch devices.

- **Recipe:** `any-pointer-coarse:text-base` on default and larger sizes. Text fields use it at every size, including `sm`.
- **Why:** 16px is readable at arm's length, and iOS zooms the page when a focused field is smaller.
- **Exceptions:** `xs` and `sm` buttons, toggles and tabs keep their size.

### SIZ-5 Touch hit area

A control smaller than 44px gets an invisible 44px hit area on touch devices.

- **Recipe:** `any-pointer-coarse:after:absolute any-pointer-coarse:after:size-full any-pointer-coarse:after:min-h-11 any-pointer-coarse:after:min-w-11`, or `after:-inset-*` for a fixed shape. Keyed on pointer capability, never on a breakpoint.
- **Standard:** `STD-A5`, `STD-K6`
- **Exceptions:** Tabs tab: 36px on touch. The scrolling tab list clips an overflowing hit area, and a 44px track would stand taller than the buttons beside it.

### SIZ-6 Icons

- **Recipe:** `[&_svg]:pointer-events-none [&_svg]:shrink-0 [&_svg:not([class*='size-'])]:size-4`. Steps: `size-3` (xs), `size-3.5` (sm), `size-4`, `size-4.5` (xl).
- **Why:** an icon keeps its size in a shrinking row, never swallows a click, and a user's `size-*` class still wins.

### SIZ-7 List popups

- **Recipe:** popup `p-1`, `sideOffset` 4; menus `min-w-32`; Select, Combobox and Autocomplete `min-w-(--anchor-width)`; item `px-2 py-1 gap-2 text-sm`; group label `px-2 py-1.5 text-xs font-medium text-muted-foreground`.
- **Exceptions:** Menubar and Navigation Menu: larger `sideOffset`, to clear their bar.

### SIZ-8 Text parts

- **Recipe:** title `text-base leading-snug font-medium`; label `text-sm leading-snug font-medium`; description `text-muted-foreground text-sm text-pretty`; links inside a description `underline underline-offset-3 hover:text-foreground`.
- **Applies to:** titles and descriptions in Dialog, Alert Dialog, Sheet and Drawer; labels in Field and Label.
- **Exceptions:** Popover: its title and description take the popup's `text-sm`.

### SIZ-9 Tracks

- **Recipe:** Progress and Slider `h-1`; Meter `h-2`.
- **Why:** a meter is a standing reading with level colours, read at a glance, so it gets more area.

### SIZ-10 Changing numbers use tabular figures

- **Recipe:** `tabular-nums` on values that update in place.
- **Applies to:** Number Field, Slider value, Progress and Meter values, Pagination, table numbers, chart tooltips.

# Motion

### MOT-1 Curves and durations

- **Recipe:** `ease-out-quint` (`cubic-bezier(0.23, 1, 0.32, 1)`) for anything that enters, exits, moves or scales; Tailwind `ease-out` for colour, border and shadow changes; `ease-drawer` (`cubic-bezier(0.32, 0.72, 0, 1)`) for edge panels. Press scale shares its control's `duration-150 ease-out`. Nothing runs longer than 300ms except edge panels, the stacked toast and looping progress.
- **Standard:** `STD-M4`, `STD-M5`

### MOT-2 List every transitioned property

- **Recipe:** `transition-[scale,opacity]`, `transition-[background-color,border-color,box-shadow]`, or a named group such as `transition-colors`. Never `transition-all`.
- **Why:** `all` animates properties nobody chose, including layout.
- **Standard:** `STD-M2`

### MOT-3 Popups scale and fade from their trigger

- **Recipe:** Base UI starting and ending styles: `origin-(--transform-origin) transition-[scale,opacity] ease-out-quint duration-150 data-ending-style:duration-100 data-starting-style:opacity-0 data-ending-style:opacity-0`. Scale `0.95` for list popups, `0.98` for content popups. Add `data-instant:transition-none` wherever the primitive sets `data-instant`.
- **Applies to:** list popups and content popups.
- **Standard:** `STD-M6`, `STD-M7`, `STD-M8`
- **Exceptions:** submenus: opacity only, 100ms. Select aligned over its trigger: no transition, a popup that covers its trigger does not grow from it. Navigation Menu: 200ms in, 150ms out, it is a larger surface that changes size. Popover, Preview Card and Navigation Menu also transition `width` and `height` from the primitive's measured variables when their content swaps, and their positioners follow the anchor.

### MOT-4 Popups driven by typing do not animate

- **Applies to:** Combobox, Autocomplete, the Phone Input country list, Command Dialog. Menubar opens instantly and only fades out.
- **Why:** the popup opens and closes on every keystroke; motion there is noise.
- **Standard:** `STD-M1`

### MOT-5 Modals

- **Recipe:** Dialog and Alert Dialog: `ease-out-quint`, 200ms in, 150ms out, scale `0.96` with opacity.
- **Standard:** `STD-M6`

### MOT-6 Edge panels

- **Recipe:** `ease-drawer`, 400ms in, 250ms out, moved with `translate`. Applies to Sheet, Drawer and the bottom mode of Dialog and Alert Dialog on small screens.
- **Why:** a panel that travels its own height needs more time than a popup, and one curve for every edge panel keeps them related.
- **Exceptions:** Drawer: 450ms in and an exit scaled by swipe strength; it animates `transform`, because it composes translate and scale from swipe variables.

### MOT-7 A backdrop shares its panel's timing

- **Recipe:** the backdrop carries the same ease class and the same in and out durations as the panel it sits behind.
- **Standard:** `STD-M11`

### MOT-8 Expand and collapse

- **Recipe:** the panel height from the Base UI variable, for example `h-(--accordion-panel-height) transition-[height] ease-out-quint duration-200 data-starting-style:h-0 data-ending-style:h-0 data-ending-style:duration-150`.
- **Applies to:** Accordion, Collapsible.
- **Why:** exits never start slow, so closing stays on an ease-out curve.

### MOT-9 Control state changes

- **Recipe:** colour, border and shadow: `duration-150 ease-out`. Check marks and radio dots appear instantly.
- **Exceptions:** Switch: 200ms `ease-out-quint`, so the track colour stays in step with the thumb.

### MOT-10 Hover easing

An isolated control eases its hover at 150ms. A member of a dense repeated set does not.

- **Applies to:** eased: Button, Toggle, standalone triggers. Instant: list items, table rows, Menubar triggers, Sidebar buttons, Calendar days, links inside a navigation popup.
- **Why:** moving the pointer down a list should not leave a trail of fading highlights.

### MOT-11 Progress and loading

- **Recipe:** Progress `transition-[width] duration-300 ease-out`; Meter the same, plus `background-color` for its level colour. Indeterminate progress loops at 1.5s. Spinner 800ms linear. Skeleton 2s linear.

### MOT-12 Reduced motion

Remove movement and scale; keep opacity and colour.

- **Recipe:** popups `motion-reduce:transition-opacity motion-reduce:data-starting-style:scale-100 motion-reduce:data-ending-style:scale-100`; edge panels fade with `motion-reduce:duration-200 motion-reduce:data-ending-style:duration-150` instead of sliding; height reveals drop the height transition (`motion-reduce:transition-none`, or `motion-reduce:transition-opacity` when the panel also fades); press scale always under `motion-safe:`. The library sets no smooth scrolling.
- **Standard:** `STD-M9`
- **Exceptions:** Spinner: keeps spinning, it is status feedback. Swipe-to-dismiss on Toast and Drawer: direct manipulation follows the finger.

### MOT-13 Keyboard shortcuts skip animation

- **Recipe:** a state change triggered by a shortcut is instant (`data-instant` or `transition-none`).
- **Applies to:** Sidebar toggle shortcut.
- **Standard:** `STD-M1`

### MOT-14 Page-level layout moves with translate

- **Recipe:** an off-canvas panel slides with `translate`; the content beside it transitions with the panel, on the same curve and duration, instead of snapping.
- **Applies to:** Sidebar.
- **Standard:** `STD-M3`

# Content

A component is fixed where plausible data makes content unreadable or unreachable: file names, emails, URLs, paths, long names, large counts. Layout choices for unusual content, such as a very long button label, stay with the app.

### CON-1 Text that can be long must be able to shrink

- **Recipe:** `min-w-0` on the flex child that holds text; `minmax(0,1fr)` or `grid-cols-1` for grid tracks that hold text; `shrink-0` on the icons, buttons and badges beside it.
- **Why:** flex and grid children default to their content width, so one long word widens the whole component.
- **Standard:** `STD-W2`

### CON-2 Titles and descriptions break long words

- **Recipe:** `wrap-break-word` on titles and descriptions. `wrap-anywhere` where the text sits in a grid or flex item that keeps its minimum content width.
- **Applies to:** Dialog, Alert Dialog, Popover, Card, Alert, Toast, Tooltip, and item text in Select, Combobox and Menubar.
- **Standard:** `STD-W1`

### CON-3 Single-line values truncate

- **Recipe:** `min-w-0 truncate` on the label, in its own element when the parent is a flex row.
- **Applies to:** Combobox chips, Input Group text, Sidebar labels.
- **Standard:** `STD-W2`

### CON-4 Popups stay inside the viewport

- **Recipe:** `max-h-(--available-height)` with `overflow-y-auto` on every positioned popup; `max-w-(--available-width)` on popups whose content sets their width.
- **Applies to:** height: every positioned popup. Width: Select, Combobox, Autocomplete, Popover, Preview Card, Navigation Menu, Tooltip.
- **Standard:** `STD-W3`

### CON-5 Counts keep their shape up to three digits

- **Recipe:** a minimum width with `w-auto px-1` in place of a fixed square (for example `min-w-8 w-auto px-1`), so the control grows only when it has to.
- **Applies to:** Pagination links, Sidebar badge.
- **Standard:** `STD-W4`

### CON-6 Left to the app

Not fixed in components, on purpose:

- Wrapping of long Button, Badge and Tab labels.
- Overflow of a Menubar or Toolbar with too many items.
- First-line alignment of a control beside a wrapped label.

- **Why:** each is a layout decision with more than one right answer, and a default would get in the way of the others.

# Right-to-left

Every component works in right-to-left layouts.

### RTL-1 Logical utilities

- **Recipe:** `ps-*`, `pe-*`, `ms-*`, `me-*`, `start-*`, `end-*`, `text-start`, `text-end`, `border-s`, `border-e`, `rounded-s-*`, `rounded-e-*` in place of the left and right forms. Use an `rtl:` variant only where no logical utility exists, for example rotation and translation.
- **Why:** logical classes compile to the same values in left-to-right, so nothing changes for existing layouts.
- **Standard:** `STD-W6`
- **Exceptions:** Phone Input: physical padding on the number field under `rtl:`. The number field stays left-to-right inside a right-to-left group, so logical padding would follow the field's own direction and land on the wrong side.

### RTL-2 Popups take their direction from `dir`

- **Recipe:** a popup wrapper accepts `dir` and passes it to its Positioner, so `align="start"` and `side="inline-start"` follow the reading direction.
- **Applies to:** Popover, Tooltip, Preview Card, Menu, Context Menu, Menubar, Navigation Menu, Select, Combobox, Autocomplete.
- **Why:** portaled content does not inherit direction from the place it was opened.

### RTL-3 Direction-aware behaviour reads the provider

- **Recipe:** `useDirection()` from Base UI for anything computed in JavaScript: scroll direction, arrow keys, slide order.
- **Applies to:** Carousel, Calendar.

### RTL-4 Physical props stay physical

A prop that names a physical edge is not mirrored.

- **Applies to:** Sheet `side`, Toast `position`, Drawer `swipeDirection`.
- **Why:** "right" means the right edge of the screen in every language. Use `inline-start` and `inline-end` where a logical side is offered.

### RTL-5 Keyboard shortcuts keep keycap order

- **Recipe:** `[unicode-bidi:plaintext]` on inline shortcut text, or an inner `<span dir="ltr">` where the shortcut is a flex container; key groups keep left-to-right order.
- **Applies to:** Kbd, menu shortcuts, Command shortcut.
- **Why:** `⌘N` describes a physical keyboard, which is not mirrored.

### RTL-6 Directional icons mirror, circular ones do not

- **Recipe:** `rtl:rotate-180` (or the mirrored icon) on chevrons and arrows that mean "forward" or "back".
- **Exceptions:** Spinner and other circular indicators keep turning clockwise.

# Accessibility

### ACC-1 Scope

Components meet WCAG 2.2 level AA. Anything beyond it is reported as "nice to have" with a recommendation and is not applied unless asked for.

- **Recipe:** every accessibility finding names the success criterion it fails. No criterion, no required fix.
- **Why:** a library that adds every possible announcement and role makes choices that belong to the app.
- **Standard:** `STD-A1` to `STD-A9`

### ACC-2 Name, role and state

- **Recipe:** icon-only controls get an `aria-label`. A popup with `role="dialog"` gets a name. A disabled link keeps `role="link"` with `aria-disabled`. A trigger that collapses something sets `aria-expanded`. The current page link sets `aria-current="page"`.
- **Standard:** `STD-A4`

### ACC-3 Selected and highlighted text keeps its contrast

- **Recipe:** secondary text inside a highlighted item switches to the item's foreground: `in-data-highlighted:text-accent-foreground`.
- **Applies to:** menu shortcuts, Command shortcut, calling codes and other muted text inside list items.
- **Standard:** `STD-A1`

### ACC-4 Not supported by the library

Left to the app, on purpose:

- Forced-colors and Windows contrast themes.
- Translated default labels. A few parts ship an English `aria-label`, such as the close button; translate it in your copy of the component.

- **Why:** both depend on the app's audience, and neither is required at level AA.

# Code

### COD-1 Component shape

- **Recipe:** function declarations; no `forwardRef`, `ref` arrives as a prop; one file per component family in `components/ui/`.

### COD-2 Imports

- **Recipe:** `import { X as BaseX } from "@base-ui/react/x"`; `import type * as React from "react"` unless the file uses hooks; lucide icons with the `Icon` suffix (`ChevronDownIcon`).

### COD-3 Prop typing

A styled part types `className` as a string. An unstyled part uses the primitive's props as they are.

- **Recipe:** styled `Omit<BaseX.Part.Props, "className"> & { className?: string }`; unstyled the primitive's own props (`BaseX.Part.Props` or `React.ComponentProps<typeof BaseX.Part>`). Keep the primitive's generics (`BaseX.Root.Props<Payload>`).
- **Why:** Base UI also accepts a function for `className`. `cn()` drops a function without an error, so the type must not accept it.
- **Standard:** `STD-K2`

### COD-4 `"use client"` only where needed

- **Recipe:** add it when the file itself uses hooks, context or event handlers. Leave it off files that only compose parts. Demos that use hooks or handlers declare it themselves.
- **Why:** a needless directive turns exported helpers such as `buttonVariants()` into client references that throw when called from a Server Component.
- **Standard:** `STD-K3`

### COD-5 Every rendered element has a `data-slot`

- **Recipe:** `data-slot="{component}-{part}"`, unique per part (`dialog-close` and `dialog-close-button` are two slots).
- **Why:** slots are the stable hook for styling a part from a parent, and for selectors such as `has-data-[slot=card-footer]`.

### COD-6 `className` and props always reach the element

- **Recipe:** `className={cn("base classes", className)}` then `{...props}`, on every branch that renders.
- **Why:** a branch that forgets either silently ignores what the user passed.
- **Standard:** `STD-K1`

### COD-7 Variants

- **Recipe:** `cva` when a part has several variant axes, a plain class map when it has one; defaults repeated in the destructure (`variant = "default"`); `data-variant` and `data-size` always emitted; size unions ordered `"sm" | "default" | "lg"`.
- **Why:** the data attributes let a parent style by variant, and they are only reliable when they are always present.

### COD-8 Popup wrappers bundle their parts

- **Recipe:** one `XPopup` renders Portal, Positioner and Popup. It accepts `align`, `alignOffset`, `side`, `sideOffset`, `anchor`, `dir` and `portalProps`.
- **Applies to:** every positioned popup.
- **Exceptions:** Context Menu: no offset defaults, it opens at the pointer.

### COD-9 Part names

- **Recipe:** `Popup` for the surface, `Panel` for a scrolling body, `Backdrop` for the layer behind a modal.
- **Exceptions:** parts that mirror a third-party library keep its names (Vaul `Content`, `Overlay`).

### COD-10 Vocabulary

- **Recipe:** `destructive` for actions (Button, menu items); `danger` for status (Badge, Alert); Toast keeps `error`, matching the toast API people know. Optional chrome uses `show*` booleans (`showArrow`, `showCloseButton`, `showHandle`), never `hide*` or a bare name. `active`, not `isActive`. Exported hooks are prefixed with their component (`useComboboxFilter`).
- **Why:** one word per idea across the library.

### COD-11 Exports

- **Recipe:** a single sorted `export { … }` block at the end of the file; types in a separate `export type { … }` line above it.

### COD-12 Ancestor selectors use named groups

- **Recipe:** `group/number-field` on the root and `group-data-[size=sm]/number-field:` on the part, in place of `in-data-[size=sm]:`.
- **Why:** an unnamed ancestor selector also matches unrelated parents that set the same attribute, such as a Card with `data-size`.
- **Standard:** `STD-K4`

### COD-13 Touch behaviour is keyed on the pointer

- **Recipe:** `any-pointer-coarse:` for anything that exists because of touch. Breakpoints are for layout only.
- **Why:** a touch tablet is wide, and a narrow window on a laptop has a mouse.
- **Standard:** `STD-K6`

# Registry and docs

These rules apply only to a project that publishes components through a registry and documents them, as 9ui does. In an app that only uses the components, skip this file.

### REG-1 Every component has a demo

- **Recipe:** `components/demos/<name>/<name>-demo.tsx` for the main demo, and one `<name>-<case>-demo.tsx` per documented example. A demo that uses state, effects or handlers starts with `"use client"`.

### REG-2 Demos do not repair components

- **Recipe:** a demo passes no class that every user would also have to pass. If it needs one, the fix belongs in the component.
- **Why:** people copy demos; a hidden fix in a demo becomes a bug in their app.

### REG-3 Every component has an RTL demo

- **Recipe:** `<name>-rtl-demo.tsx` with English, Arabic and Hebrew strings through `useTranslation`, shown with `<ComponentPreview name="<name>-rtl-demo" direction="rtl" />`. It shows only the cases where direction matters, and passes `dir` to portaled parts.

### REG-4 Docs page shape

- **Recipe:** in this order: links to the primitive's reference, the main preview, `## Installation`, `## Usage` (imports and anatomy), `## Examples` with one `###` per demo, `### RTL` as the last example, `## Form Integration` where the component is a form control, `## API Reference`.
- **Wording:** short and direct: "To do X, set Y." No implementation details.

### REG-5 API Reference lists only what the library adds

- **Recipe:** own props, defaults that differ from the primitive, props forwarded to a bundled part, parts that do not exist in the primitive, exported helpers. Never `className`, `children`, `render` or `ref`. A component that adds nothing gets one sentence and a link to the primitive's reference.

### REG-6 Registry entry

- **Recipe:** one item per component in `registry.json`. `dependencies` lists every package the file imports, without versions. `registryDependencies` lists every other component it imports.
- **Why:** the shadcn CLI skips an unversioned package that is already installed and re-adds a versioned one, so versions on items cause needless reinstalls.
- **Exceptions:** Checkbox Group: lists Checkbox as a registry dependency without importing it, because a group is of no use without its checkboxes.

### REG-7 Version pins live in the init

- **Recipe:** pin shared packages once, in the init item. Pin on a component only when a newer major of its package is known to break it.

### REG-8 Tokens a component needs ship with the registry

- **Recipe:** a custom easing, utility, keyframe or variable used by a component is added to the registry in the same change: on the component's own item when only that component uses it, in the init when it is shared.
- **Why:** a class that only exists on the docs site compiles to nothing in a user's project.
